post.title: Workbench: Two Engines, One UI
post.hook: Claude Code, dressed up as a Codex server so one desktop app can drive both.
post.summary: Workbench is an Electron desktop app with Codex and Claude as interchangeable engines behind one UI. A custom claude-app-server maps the Claude Agent SDK onto the Codex app-server JSON-RPC protocol.
post.writeup:
## What it is
Workbench is a Codex-style desktop app built with Electron, React and Vite. It has two interchangeable engines behind a single UI: the real `codex app-server`, and `claude-app-server`, a process written in this repo that puts Claude Code behind the same wire format.

## Why
Rather than build two clients, the app speaks one protocol: the Codex app-server JSON-RPC (v2), newline-delimited over stdio. The Electron app then needs only one client, one transcript reducer and one set of components. Each thread is pinned to the engine it started on, and thread keys are `engine:threadId` because ids are only unique within one engine.

## How it works
`claude-app-server` implements the subset of the protocol Workbench uses and translates each call to the Claude Agent SDK. `thread/start` becomes a new UUID used as the `sessionId`, `thread/resume` becomes `resume: threadId`, and `turn/start` becomes one `query()` per turn with partial messages for deltas. `turn/interrupt` is an `AbortController.abort()`. Tool use maps to items: `Bash` becomes a `commandExecution`, `Edit`/`MultiEdit`/`Write` become `fileChange`, and approvals flow through the `canUseTool` callback.

Access presets (Read only, Ask, Agent, Full access) map to SDK permission modes: `plan`, `default`, `acceptEdits` and `bypassPermissions`. A shared reducer turns notifications into a transcript, which main persists as JSON and the renderer draws. A git panel shows working-tree diffs the same way for both engines.

## Status
The pieces are all in place: engine spawning, persistence, approvals, diff panel and the standalone server, which can also run on its own with `node out/main/claude-app-server.js`. There are no benchmarks or tests in the material.

## Open questions
How much of the Codex protocol surface Claude can honestly cover, and how the two engines compare on the same task, are not yet answered.
